Q: What is physical destruction in the context of data disposal?
Option1: Physically damaging media so it cannot be used again
Option2: Deleting files through the recycle bin
Option4: Compressing the drive to save space

Q: What is drilling as a destruction method?
Option1: Boring holes through platters or chips to prevent data access
Option3: Removing the drive from the chassis
Option4: Powering the device on and off repeatedly

Q: What does shredding do to storage media?
Option1: Cuts media into small pieces to make recovery impractical
Option3: Heats media to a set temperature

Q: What is degaussing primarily used for?
Option1: Disrupting magnetic fields on magnetic media such as hard drives and tapes
Option2: Securely erasing solid state drives by controller command

Q: Which media is not effectively sanitized by degaussing?
Option1: Solid state drives

Q: What is incinerating in disposal?
Option1: Destroying media by controlled burning

Q: What is meant by erasing or wiping a drive?
Option1: Overwriting data areas with known patterns or zeros
Option3: Moving files to a hidden folder

Q: What does low level formatting mean on modern systems?
Option1: A vendor or tool driven overwrite of all addressable blocks
Option2: A quick format that rebuilds only the file system table
Option3: A firmware setting for boot order

Q: What is standard formatting?
Option1: Recreating file system structures without guaranteed data wipe

Q: Which option best ensures no customer data remains before recycling a PC?
Option1: Full device wipe or secure erase that overwrites all blocks

Q: What is the safest approach for failed hard drives containing sensitive data?
Option1: Physical destruction and documented disposal
Option3: Ship to user home for testing

Q: What is a third party vendor in disposal workflows?
Option1: An external company contracted to destroy or recycle media

Q: What is a certificate of destruction?
Option1: Documented proof that specific assets were destroyed or recycled

Q: Why is a chain of custody important during disposal?
Option1: It proves who handled assets at each step to reduce risk of data leakage
Option4: It encrypts the media in transit

Q: Which method best prevents reuse of a laptop with high risk data?
Option1: Remove and shred storage media and crush the laptop chassis
Option2: Log off and leave the login screen

Q: A company plans to donate used PCs. What should be done first?
Option1: Wipe or secure erase drives and verify results
Option2: Move data to an external drive and hand off PCs
Option3: Create a new local admin and keep old accounts

Q: What is the primary risk of using only standard formatting before resale?
Option1: Residual data may be recoverable with tools
Option4: Operating system will not install apps

Q: Which control verifies that a wipe completed successfully?
Option1: Validation logs or spot checks with forensic tools
Option3: Ask users if files are gone

Q: Why might an organization choose degaussing followed by shredding for hard disk drives?
Option1: Defense in depth to ensure magnetic data and the media are destroyed

Q: What is recommended for sanitizing a solid state drive that will be reused internally?
Option1: Controller secure erase or vendor tool for the specific drive
Option2: Run a magnet over the case
Option3: Drill one hole through the label

Q: What should be documented when outsourcing disposal?
Option1: Asset IDs, date, method, vendor, certificate of destruction, and witnesses if required
Option2: Brand of drill used and paint color of the truck

Q: A user reformats a USB drive and gives it to a coworker. Sensitive files were on it. What policy was missed?
Option1: Proper sanitization by wipe or destruction and approval before reuse

Q: Which option best balances environmental concerns and data security for bulk hard disk drives with medium sensitivity?
Option1: Certified recycling with verified wipe and sample validation
Option3: Keep in a box for future use

Q: What is the difference between wipe and format for data disposal?
Option1: Wipe overwrites data areas; format rebuilds the file system and may leave data recoverable
Option3: Format is more secure than wipe

Q: Why is vendor secure erase preferred for solid state drives?
Option1: It targets all flash blocks, including those not mapped to the file system
Option3: It edits only the partition table

Q: Which document proves compliant third party destruction?
Option1: Certificate of destruction tied to asset IDs
